questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If α and β are the zeroes of polynomial 3x² + 6x + k such that α + β + αβ = −2/3, then the value of k is :
questions.solution: α + β = −6/3 = −2 and αβ = k/3. So −2 + k/3 = −2/3, which gives k/3 = 4/3 and k = 4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.text: If x = 1 and y = 2 is a solution of the pair of linear equations 2x − 3y + a = 0 and 2x + 3y − b = 0, then :
questions.solution: Put x = 1, y = 2. First equation: 2 − 6 + a = 0, so a = 4. Second: 2 + 6 − b = 0, so b = 8. Hence 2a = b.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The mid-point of the line segment joining the points P(−4, 5) and Q(4, 6) lies on :
questions.solution: Mid-point = ((−4 + 4)/2, (5 + 6)/2) = (0, 11/2). Its x-coordinate is 0, so it lies on the y-axis.

questions.text: In triangles ABC and DEF, ∠B = ∠E, ∠F = ∠C and AB = 3 DE. Then, the two triangles are :
questions.solution: Two pairs of equal angles make the triangles similar (AA). Since AB = 3 DE, the sides are not equal, so they are not congruent.

questions.text: If (−1)ⁿ + (−1)⁸ = 0, then n is :
questions.solution: (−1)⁸ = 1, so (−1)ⁿ = −1. This happens exactly when n is odd.

questions.text: If the sum of first m terms of an AP is 2m² + 3m, then its second term is :
questions.solution: S₁ = 2 + 3 = 5 and S₂ = 8 + 6 = 14. Second term = S₂ − S₁ = 9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Mode and Mean of a data are 15x and 18x, respectively. Then the median of the data is :
questions.solution: Using Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean: 15x = 3 Median − 36x, so 3 Median = 51x and Median = 17x.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A card is selected at random from a deck of 52 playing cards. The probability of it being a red face card is :
questions.solution: There are 6 red face cards (J, Q, K of hearts and diamonds). P = 6/52 = 3/26.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): If we join two hemispheres of same radius along their bases, then we get a sphere.
Reason (R): Total Surface Area of a sphere of radius r is 3πr².
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Two equal hemispheres joined at their bases do form a sphere, so A is true. The surface area of a sphere is 4πr², not 3πr², so R is false.

questions.text: Evaluate : tan²60° / (sin²60° + cos²30°)
questions.solution: tan²60° = (√3)² = 3. sin²60° = 3/4 and cos²30° = 3/4, so the denominator is 3/2. Value = 3 ÷ 3/2 = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If Δ ABC ~ Δ PQR in which AB = 6 cm, BC = 4 cm, AC = 8 cm and PR = 6 cm, then find the length of (PQ + QR).
questions.solution: For similar triangles AB/PQ = BC/QR = AC/PR = 8/6 = 4/3. So PQ = 6 × 3/4 = 4.5 cm and QR = 4 × 3/4 = 3 cm. PQ + QR = 7.5 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A person is standing at P outside a circular ground at a distance of 26 m from the centre of the ground. He found that his distances from the points A and B on the ground are 10 m (PA and PB are tangents to the circle). Find the radius of the circular ground.
questions.solution: The radius OA is perpendicular to the tangent PA, so triangle OAP is right-angled at A. OA² = OP² − PA² = 26² − 10² = 676 − 100 = 576, so the radius is 24 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that opposite sides of a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle subtend supplementary angles at the centre of the circle.
questions.solution: Let ABCD circumscribe a circle with centre O, touching AB, BC, CD, DA at P, Q, R, S. Tangents from an external point are equal and OA, OB, OC, OD bisect the angles between the radii at each vertex, so ∠AOP = ∠AOS, ∠BOP = ∠BOQ, ∠COQ = ∠COR and ∠DOR = ∠DOS. These eight angles add up to 360°, so 2(∠AOP + ∠BOP + ∠COR + ∠DOR) = 360°, i.e. ∠AOB + ∠COD = 180°. In the same way ∠BOC + ∠AOD = 180°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that : tan θ/(1 − cot θ) + cot θ/(1 − tan θ) = 1 + sec θ cosec θ
questions.solution: Let t = tan θ, so cot θ = 1/t. LHS = t/(1 − 1/t) + (1/t)/(1 − t) = t²/(t − 1) − 1/(t(t − 1)) = (t³ − 1)/(t(t − 1)) = (t² + t + 1)/t = t + 1 + 1/t. Now t + 1/t = sin θ/cos θ + cos θ/sin θ = 1/(sin θ cos θ) = sec θ cosec θ. So LHS = 1 + sec θ cosec θ.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that : (sin A + cos A)/(sin A − cos A) + (sin A − cos A)/(sin A + cos A) = 2/(2 sin²A − 1)
questions.solution: LHS = [(sin A + cos A)² + (sin A − cos A)²] / (sin²A − cos²A) = 2(sin²A + cos²A) / (sin²A − cos²A) = 2 / (sin²A − (1 − sin²A)) = 2/(2 sin²A − 1).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the ratio in which the y-axis divides the line segment joining the points (5, −6) and (−1, −4). Also find the point of intersection.
questions.solution: Let the ratio be k : 1. On the y-axis x = 0, so (−k + 5)/(k + 1) = 0 and k = 5. The ratio is 5 : 1. y = (5 × (−4) + 1 × (−6))/6 = −26/6 = −13/3. The point is (0, −13/3).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that 1/√5 is an irrational number.
questions.solution: First, √5 is irrational: if √5 = a/b with a, b coprime, then a² = 5b², so 5 divides a; writing a = 5c gives b² = 5c², so 5 divides b too, a contradiction. Now suppose 1/√5 = p/q is rational (p, q integers, p ≠ 0). Then √5 = q/p would be rational, which is false. So 1/√5 is irrational.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A room is in the form of a cylinder surmounted by a hemispherical dome. The base radius of the hemisphere is half of the height of the cylindrical part. If the room contains 1408/21 m³ of air, find the height of the cylindrical part. (Use π = 22/7).
questions.solution: Let the radius be r, so the cylinder's height is 2r. Volume = πr²(2r) + (2/3)πr³ = (8/3)πr³ = (8/3)(22/7)r³ = (176/21)r³. Setting (176/21)r³ = 1408/21 gives r³ = 8, so r = 2 m. The height of the cylindrical part is 4 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two dice are thrown at the same time. Determine the probability that the difference of the numbers on the two dice is 2.
questions.solution: There are 36 equally likely outcomes. Difference 2: (1, 3), (3, 1), (2, 4), (4, 2), (3, 5), (5, 3), (4, 6), (6, 4), which is 8 outcomes. P = 8/36 = 2/9.

questions.text: Vijay invested certain amounts of money in two schemes A and B, which offer interest at the rate of 8% per annum and 9% per annum, respectively. He received ₹1,860 as the total annual interest. However, had he interchanged the amounts of investments in the two schemes, he would have received ₹20 more as annual interest. How much money did he invest in each scheme ?
questions.solution: Let ₹x be in A and ₹y in B. 8x/100 + 9y/100 = 1860 gives 8x + 9y = 186000. Interchanged: 9x + 8y = 188000. Adding: 17(x + y) = 374000, so x + y = 22000. Subtracting: x − y = 2000. So x = 12000 and y = 10000. He invested ₹12,000 in scheme A and ₹10,000 in scheme B. (Check: 960 + 900 = 1860.)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The diagonal BD of a parallelogram ABCD intersects the line segment AE at the point F, where E is any point on the side BC. Prove that DF × EF = FB × FA.
questions.solution: In Δ AFD and Δ EFB: ∠DAF = ∠BEF (alternate angles, since AD ∥ BC and AE is a transversal) and ∠AFD = ∠EFB (vertically opposite angles). So Δ AFD ~ Δ EFB (AA). Hence FA/FE = FD/FB, which gives DF × EF = FB × FA.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In Δ ABC, if AD ⊥ BC and AD² = BD × DC, then prove that ∠BAC = 90°.
questions.solution: AD² = BD × DC gives AD/BD = DC/AD. Also ∠ADB = ∠CDA = 90°. So Δ ADB ~ Δ CDA (SAS similarity), and ∠BAD = ∠ACD. In right Δ ADC, ∠DAC + ∠ACD = 90°. So ∠BAC = ∠BAD + ∠DAC = ∠ACD + ∠DAC = 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The perimeter of a right triangle is 60 cm and its hypotenuse is 25 cm. Find the lengths of other two sides of the triangle.
questions.solution: Let the sides be x and 35 − x (since x + (35 − x) + 25 = 60). By Pythagoras, x² + (35 − x)² = 625, so 2x² − 70x + 1225 = 625, i.e. x² − 35x + 300 = 0. This factorises as (x − 15)(x − 20) = 0. The other two sides are 15 cm and 20 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A train travels a distance of 480 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 8 km/h less, then it would have taken 3 hours more to cover the same distance. Find the speed of the train.
questions.solution: Let the speed be x km/h. 480/(x − 8) − 480/x = 3, so 480 × 8 = 3x(x − 8), i.e. x² − 8x − 1280 = 0. This factorises as (x − 40)(x + 32) = 0. Speed cannot be negative, so the speed is 40 km/h.

questions.text:
A school is organizing a charity run to raise funds for a local hospital. The run is planned as a series of rounds around a track, with each round being 300 metres. To make the event more challenging and engaging, the organizers decide to increase the distance of each subsequent round by 50 metres. For example, the second round will be 350 metres, the third round will be 400 metres and so on. The total number of rounds planned is 10.

Write the fourth, fifth and sixth term of the Arithmetic Progression so formed.
questions.solution: a = 300 and d = 50. The 4th, 5th and 6th terms are 450 m, 500 m and 550 m.

questions.text:
One such brooch is made with silver wire in the form of a circle with diameter 35 mm. The wire is also used in making 5 diameters which divide the circle into 10 equal sectors.

Find the total length of the silver wire used.
questions.solution: Circumference = πd = (22/7) × 35 = 110 mm. Five diameters = 5 × 35 = 175 mm. Total wire = 110 + 175 = 285 mm.
